fact: In New York, shore anglers must cast baits with a rod and reel. No drones, no kayaks.
Florida allows drone drops, but dropping a bait with a hook 1.5 inches or larger means you need the free shore-based shark permit and the Shark-Smart course (16+).
Massachusetts bans drones, RC boats and bait cannons for deploying baits from shore, statewide.
Cape Hatteras National Seashore bans drones and bait launchers. Check which beaches are park land before you fly.
In New Jersey, knowingly using a drone to take wildlife is a disorderly persons offense. Bay Head police started applying it to drone-dropped shark baits in August 2026.
When the evening wind averages over 25 mph, the SharkLeash Drop Score caps at 40. Too windy to fly a drop.
Ocean City, MD requires baits to be cast: no kayaking or drones. Assateague Island National Seashore bans drones too.
Texas Parks and Wildlife says drone bait drops break the federal Airborne Hunting Act. No state charges, but the federal risk is yours.
Gulf Islands National Seashore (Pensacola to the Mississippi islands) bans drones. Canaveral National Seashore does too.
Louisiana law bans using any aircraft to help take finfish (R.S. 56:320(G)), and a drone drop fits that wording.
Padre Island National Seashore bans drones, with no exception for fishing.
Your drone may be legal, but the beach may not be: Virginia Beach bans shark fishing on its city beaches entirely.
